div.head: Ps Cn for 24
div.ab: Sed si regalem feram, quam Angli a staggon appellant, alteruter coegerit anhelare, alter per unum annum, alter per duos careat libertate naturali; si uero seruus, pro utlagato habeatur, quem Angli frendlæsman uocant.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 624 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: But if either of them makes a royal beast, which the English call a staggon (a stag), pant, the one shall lose his natural freedom for one year, the other for two; but if a slave, let him be held an outlaw, whom the English call frendlæsman (friendless man).
div.note: In Cn II 13.2; In Cn II 15a

note.seg: Astaggon Cii; a lacking in Ho

Twici nennt so den fünfjährigen Hirsch; Verf. meint den Hirsch allgemein; Toller Ags. dict. s. v. stacga citirt nur diese Stelle; es ist Nordisches Lehnwort. Vom hundum geswenced heorot singt schon Beowulf 1369

Twici gives this name to the five-year-old hart; the author means the hart in general; Toller, Ags. dict. s. v. stacga, cites only this passage; it is a Norse loanword. Beowulf 1369 already sings of the hundum geswenced heorot (the hart hard pressed by hounds)

vgl. Heinrichs II. Assise: nullus chaceat [seine eigenen] feras per noctem infra forestam neque extra [also auf eigenem Grunde!], ubicunque feræ [regales] frequentant, sub pena imprisonamenti unius anni ed. Stubbs Rog. Hov. II 2472. Nicht für blosse Aufstörung, sondern für captio uenationis und nur bei Zahlungsunfähigen setzt 1217 die Charta de foresta 10: iaceat in prisona annum, et [ni]si post plegios inuenire possit, abiuret regnum

cf. Henry II's Assize: nullus chaceat [his own] feras per noctem infra forestam neque extra [so on his own land!], ubicunque feræ [regales] frequentant, sub pena imprisonamenti unius anni, ed. Stubbs, Rog. Hov. II 2472. Not for mere disturbing, but for captio uenationis, and only for those unable to pay, the Charta de foresta 10 of 1217 lays down: iaceat in prisona annum, et [ni]si post plegios inuenire possit, abiuret regnum

vgl. abiuret regnum (vor. Anm.) nur noch für höchsten Jagdfrevel, während utlagati pro foresta tantum a tempore Henrici [II] ad pacem ueniant; ebd. 15. Die Friedloslegung eines Sklaven widerspricht Germanischem Strafrechte; vgl. Maurer Krit. Überschau III 55

cf. abiuret regnum (previous note), now only for the gravest hunting offence, whereas utlagati pro foresta tantum a tempore Henrici [II] ad pacem ueniant; ibid. 15. The outlawing of a slave contradicts Germanic criminal law; cf. Maurer, Krit. Überschau III 55

friðleas des Originals verwandelte ein Inst.-Schreiber vor 1200 in frendleas, o. S. 31914, ebenso wie Verf., vielleicht weil frið schon veraltete. Unserer Freundschaft verlustig nennen Eadward und Reishstag den Friedlosen II Ew. 5, 1

The friðleas of the original was changed into frendleas by a scribe of the Inst. before 1200, above p. 319 note 14, just as by the author, perhaps because frið was already becoming obsolete. Edward and the Reichstag call the outlaw 'deprived of our friendship', II Ew. 5, 1
Im späteren 13. Jh. dient befristetes Gefängnis nicht als Strafe; Turner p. lxv
In the later 13th century imprisonment for a fixed term is not used as a punishment; Turner p. lxv
